title: World Cup substitutes unlikely to face punishment for celebrating goals on pitch
content:
World Cup substitutes are unlikely to face punishment for running onto the pitch to celebrate a goal with their team-mates.

In three of the four group stage matches on Friday, substitutes entered the field of play to join in the jubilant scenes.

This followed on from the USMNT’s opening win over Paraguay on June 12, which saw head coach Mauricio Pochettino and multiple substitutes running onto the pitch to celebrate Gio Reyna’s excellent strike.

Several U.S. substitutes, who were waiting to run on during a VAR check, also joined in the celebrations on Friday night in Seattle, when the referee Felix Zwayer confirmed Alex Freeman’s goal against Australia will stand.

Although match officials can discipline a substitute for entering the field of play without permission, the International Football Association Board’s (IFAB) rulebook states that they “must only stop play” if there is an “interference with the play”.

In similar scenes to both USMNT fixtures, Brazil’s Vinicius Junior was joined by players from the bench to celebrate his goal against Haiti in Philadelphia.

And in Paraguay’s win over Turkey on Friday night, Matias Galarza’s early strike was met with the national team’s substitute pouring onto the pitch.

Even though the match officials are unlikely to dish out any yellow cards, as the celebrations are not interfering with play, they are mindful of the elapsed time between the goal being scored and play restarting and will ensure it is added on at the end of the half.

There were similar celebration scenes at the 2022 Qatar World Cup, although — as is the case during this tournament — not every national team is doing it.
